source.title: Increased decision thresholds enhance information gathering performance in juvenile Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder (OCD)

confidence_rationale: The clean clinical-computational anchor for the epistemic-freezing pole and the exact mirror of the Ross 2015 jumping-to-conclusions finding: OCD youth set HIGHER decision thresholds and gather MORE information before committing, modelled as an altered cost of sampling. Together with the JTC entry it brackets the commitment-timing axis from both ends -- under-gather (panic/JTC) vs over-gather (freezing/OCD). Confidence 0.70: rigorous model-based clinical study, but the over-gathering is in an abstract sampling task, and 'enhanced performance' shows the pole is not purely pathological (context-dependent).
failure_signatures: Epistemic-freezing: a raised decision threshold / increased subjective cost of committing produces extended information gathering and delayed (or absent) commitment -- the over-exploration pole MECH-434 must bound.
The effect can be advantageous in some contexts, so the axis is a trade-off with an optimal band, not a deficit to minimise to zero.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Juvenile OCD patients gather more information before deciding than controls; computational modelling attributes this to an increased decision threshold arising from an altered (lowered) perceived cost of sampling, which in some contexts yields better-informed, more accurate decisions.
mapping.ree_translation: Grounds the epistemic-freezing pole of MECH-434 and completes the symmetry with anti-epistemic-panic: where panic collapses the threshold (commit too early), freezing raises it (gather forever). Maps the axis onto a concrete, dimensional clinical parameter (decision threshold / sampling cost) -- the same knob Cisek's urgency gating modulates from the other side -- and shows it is graded and context-sensitive, supporting MECH-434's inverted-U / optimal-band framing.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The beads-like sequential sampling task is abstract and human; generalising 'decision threshold / sampling cost' to REE's belief-state commitment over inferred trajectories is a functional mapping, not a shared mechanism. And 'enhanced performance' warns against treating the freezing pole as purely pathological.
mapping.source_context: Computational-psychiatry study: juvenile OCD vs controls on a sequential information-sampling task, fit with a Bayesian/cost-of-sampling decision model.

confidence_components.notes: Rigorous computational-psychiatry source. Mapping fidelity moderate (abstract sampling task -> REE commitment); the context-dependent benefit is itself informative about the axis being a trade-off.
